parole.testo: From German Zirkon (“zircon mineral”) via French zircon, formed in the 1780s from Arabic زَرْقُون (zarqūn, “zircon, minium”), from Middle Persian 𐭦𐭫𐭢𐭥𐭭 (zlgʿn /⁠zargōn⁠/), from Classical Persian زرگون (zargōn)/Middle Persian 𐭦𐭫𐭢𐭥𐭭 (zlgʿn /⁠zargōn⁠/, “red lead”), from Proto-Iranian *jr̥Hanyam (“gold”
From ημί- (imí-) + φως (fos), a calque of German Halblicht and French demi-jour.

parole.significato: of or related to percussion instruments
parole.testo: From Hellenistic Koine Greek κρουστός, and a semantic loan from German Schlaginstrumente or French instruments à percussion.

Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek μετάθεσις (metáthesis, “change of position”) with, in the sense 'transfer', semantic loan from German Versetzung and French déplacement. By surface analysis, μεταθέτω (metathéto) + -ση (-si).
Learned borrowing from German Ökologie or French écologie. By surface analysis, οικο- (oiko-) + -λογία (-logía).
Learned borrowing from German ökologisch and French écologique. By surface analysis, οικολογία (oikología) + -ικός (-ikós).
Nominalized learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp”) with semantic loan from German Säure and French acide.
Semantic loan from German Lehnübersetzung and French emprunt. Also see μεταφραστικό δάνειο (metaphrastikó dáneio, “translation loan”).

parole.significato: to coordinate, effect by concerted or joint effort
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Koine Greek σῠντονίᾱ (sŭntoníā, “harmony (of sounds; (ancient) intensity”) + -ίζω (-ízo), with semantic loan from German abstimmen (“(reflexive) to synchronize”). For the "syntonize" meaning, reborrowing and semantic loan from French syntoniser.
